questions.q: Due to their extensive rice cultivation, some regions may be contributing to global warming. To what possible reason/reasons is this attributable? [2010] 1️⃣ The anaerobic conditions associated with rice cultivation cause the emission of methane. 2️⃣ When nitrogen based fertilizers are used, nitrous oxide is emitted from the cultivated soil.
questions.e: Methane and nitrous oxide are the two greenhouse gases emitted from rice fields. Flooding cuts off the oxygen supply from the atmosphere, resulting in anaerobic conditions which emit methane. Nitrogen fertilizers used for high production emit nitrous oxide by reacting with atmospheric oxygen.

questions.q: Within biological communities, some species are important in determining the ability of a large number of other species to persist in the community. Such species are called [2000]
questions.e: A keystone species is a species that plays a critical role in maintaining the structure of an ecological community. Its impact in the community is much greater than would be expected based on its relative abundance or total biomass.

questions.q: Consider the following animals of India: [2003] 1️⃣ Crocodile 2️⃣ Elephant. Which of these is/are endangered species?
questions.e: According to the source, only the crocodile is kept in the Red Book or endangered species list among the options provided.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2005] 1️⃣ Kyoto protocol came into force in the year 2005. 2️⃣ Kyoto protocol deals primarily with the depletion of the ozone layer. 3️⃣ Methane as a greenhouse gas is more harmful than carbon dioxide. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Kyoto Protocol entered into force on 16th February 2005. It deals with reducing greenhouse gas emissions to a level at least 5% below 1990 levels, while the Montreal Protocol deals with ozone depletion. Methane is more effective or harmful as a greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2008] 1️⃣ Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) in respect of carbon credits is one of the Kyoto Protocol Mechanisms. 2️⃣ Under the CDM, the projects handled pertain only to the Annex-I countries. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The CDM is defined in Article 12 of the Kyoto Protocol. It is intended to assist non-Annex I parties (developing countries) in achieving sustainable development and Annex I parties (developed countries) in achieving compliance with their emission reduction commitments.

questions.q: Where was the World Summit on Sustainable Development (Rio+10) held? [2008]
questions.e: The United Nations World Summit on Sustainable Development (Rio+10) took place in Johannesburg, South Africa. It was conducted between 26 August and 4 September 2002.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2008] 1️⃣ Salt-water crocodile is found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. 2️⃣ Shrew and tapir are found in the Western Ghats of the Malabar region. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: In India, the salt-water crocodile is found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and can grow up to 6-7 meters long. However, shrew and tapir are found in the great Himalayan range, not the Western Ghats.

questions.q: The concept of carbon credit originated from which one of the following? [2009]
questions.e: The Kyoto Protocol invented the concept of carbon emissions trading, whereby carbon credits were a "flexibility mechanism." A carbon credit represents the right to emit one tonne of carbon dioxide or its equivalent.

questions.q: The National Forest Policy of 1988 includes: [1996] 1️⃣ Afforestation and development of wastelands 2️⃣ Reforestation and replantation in existing forests 3️⃣ Encouraging the wood substitutes and supplying other types of fuel 4️⃣ Promotion of wide use of insecticides and pesticides to restrict the loss of forest area from degradation caused by pests and insects.
questions.e: The National Forest Policy of 1988 describes the protection and development of forests. It emphasizes afforestation, reforestation, and wood substitutes, but it does not describe the use of insecticides and pesticides in forest areas.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: Protected area — Well-known for [2010] 1️⃣ Bhitarkanika, Orissa — Salt Water Crocodile 2️⃣ Desert National Park, Rajasthan — Great Indian Bustard 3️⃣ Eravikulam, Kerala — Hoolak Gibbon. Which of the pairs given above is / are correctly matched?
questions.e: Bhitarkanika is a protected area for salt water crocodiles. The Great Indian Bustard is protected in the desert area of Rajasthan. Eravikulam National Park was established to protect the Nilgiri Tahr, not the Hoolak Gibbon.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2010] 1️⃣ Biodiversity hotspots are located only in tropical regions. 2️⃣ India has four biodiversity hotspots i.e., Eastern Himalayas, Western Himalayas, Western Ghats and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Which of the statements given above is / are correct?
questions.e: Biodiversity hotspots are not confined only to tropical regions. India's hotspots include the Eastern Himalayas, Western Ghats, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands, but the Western Himalayas is not classified as a separate hotspot in this context.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2010] 1️⃣ The boundaries of a National Park are defined by legislation. 2️⃣ A Biosphere Reserve is declared to conserve a few specific species of flora and fauna. 3️⃣ In a Wildlife Sanctuary, limited biotic interference is permitted. Which of the statements given above is / correct?
questions.e: The boundaries of a National Park are described in the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. A Biosphere Reserve aims to conserve an entire ecosystem rather than just a few specific species. In Wildlife Sanctuaries, limited biotic interference is allowed.

questions.q: A pesticide which is a chlorinated hydrocarbon is sprayed on a food crop. The food chain is: Food crop-Rat-Snake-Hawk. In this food chain, the highest concentration of the pesticide would accumulate in which one of the following? [2010]
questions.e: Biomagnification is the increasing concentration of a compound in the tissues of organisms as it passes up a food chain. Hawk is the top consumer in this chain, so the pesticide concentration will be highest in the Hawk.

questions.q: As a result of their annual survey, the National Geographic Society and an international polling firm Globe Scan gave India top rank in Greendex 2009 score. What is this score? [2010]
o: (b) It is a measure of environmentally sustainable...
(c) It is an assessment of programmes/ schemes und...
(a) It is a measure of efforts made by different c...
(d) It is an index showing the volume of carbon cr...
questions.e: In the third annual survey of the National Geographic Society and Globe Scan, India was ranked top in Greendex 2009 due to environmentally sustainable consumer behaviour.

questions.q: India is a party to the Ramsar Convention and has declared many areas as Ramsar sites. Which of the following statements best describes as to how we should maintain these sites in the context of this convention? [2010]
o: (a) Keep all the sites completely inaccessible to...
(b) Conserve all the sites through ecosystem appro...
(c) Conserve all the sites through ecosystem appro...
(d) Conserve all the sites through ecosystem appro...
questions.e: The Ramsar Convention describes the conservation of all sites through an ecosystem approach while allowing for their simultaneous sustainable use.

questions.q: What are the possible limitations of India in mitigating the global warming at present and in the immediate future? [2010] 1️⃣ Appropriate alternate technologies are not sufficiently available. 2️⃣ India cannot invest huge funds in research and development. 3️⃣ Many developed countries have already set up their polluting industries in India.
questions.e: Mitigation in India is limited because appropriate technologies are restricted and costly. Furthermore, India lacks the massive funds required for research and development in the area of climate change mitigation.

questions.q: Consider the following which can be found in the ambient atmosphere: [2010] 1️⃣ Soot 2️⃣ Sulphur hexafluoride 3️⃣ Water vapour. Which of the above contribute to the warming up of the atmosphere?
questions.e: Ambient atmosphere refers to the surrounding conditions. Soot, sulphur hexafluoride, and water vapour can all be found in the ambient atmosphere and contribute to the warming up of the atmosphere.

questions.q: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) is an international treaty drawn at [2010]
o: (a) United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, Stockholm, 1972
(c) World Summit on Sustainable Development, Johannesburg, 2002
(b) UN Conference on Environment and Development, Rio de Janeiro, 1992
questions.e: The UNFCCC is an international treaty that was drawn at the United Nations Conference on Environment and Development held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992.

questions.q: Regarding "carbon credits", which one of the following statements is not correct? [2011-I]
o: (b) Carbon credits are awarded to countries or gro...
(d) Carbon credits are traded at a price fixed fro...
(c) The goal of the carbon credit system is to lim...
(a) The carbon credit system was ratified in conju...
questions.e: Under the Kyoto Protocol, carbon credits are part of a flexibility mechanism for trading. They represent an allowance to emit one metric tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent. The price is not fixed by the UNEP; they are traded based on market mechanisms.

questions.q: Human activities in the recent past have caused the increased concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, but a lot of it does not remain in the lower atmosphere because of [2011-I] 1️⃣ its escape into the outer stratosphere. 2️⃣ the photosynthesis by phytoplankton in the oceans. 3️⃣ the trapping of air in the polar ice caps. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Carbon dioxide is heavier than air and sinks into the ocean rather than moving to the outer stratosphere. It is also observed that CO2 is trapped in polar ice caps during winter.

questions.q: In the context of ecosystem productivity, marine upwelling zones are important as they increase the marine productivity by bringing the [2011-I] 1️⃣ decomposer microorganisms to the surface. 2️⃣ nutrients to the surface. 3️⃣ bottom-dwelling organisms to the surface. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Upwelling brings nutrient-rich water from the depths to the ocean surface. This supports phytoplankton growth and increases productivity. It has nothing to do with bringing decomposer microorganisms or bottom-dwelling organisms to the top.

questions.q: The formation of ozone hole in the Antarctic region has been a cause of concern. What could be the reason for the formation of this hole? [2011-I]
o: (d) Increased temperature at polar region due to global warming.
(b) Presence of prominent polar front and stratospheric clouds; and inflow of chlorofluorocarbons.
(c) Absence of polar front and stratospheric clouds; and inflow of methane and chlorofluorocarbons.
(a) Presence of prominent tropo-spheric turbulence; and inflow of chlorofluorocarbons.
questions.e: The formation of the ozone hole is linked to the presence of polar stratospheric clouds. Nitric acid in these clouds reacts with CFCs to release chlorine, which then catalyzes the photochemical destruction of ozone.

questions.q: Two important rivers—one with its source in Jharkhand (and known by a different name in Odisha), and another, with its source in Odisha—merge at a place only a short distance from the coast of Bay of Bengal before flowing into the sea. This is an important site of wildlife and biodiversity and a protected area. Which one of the following could be this? [2011-I]
questions.e: The Bhitarkanika Mangroves are a major wetland in Odisha, covering the river delta of the Brahmani and Baitarani rivers, which corresponds to the river descriptions provided.

questions.q: Three of the following criteria have contributed to the recognition of Western Ghats, Sri Lanka and Indo Burma regions as hotspots of biodiversity: [2011-I] 1️⃣ Species richness 2️⃣ Vegetation density 3️⃣ Endemism 4️⃣ Ethno-botanical importance 5️⃣ Threat perception 6️⃣ Adaption of flora and fauna to warm and humid conditions. Which three of the above are correct criteria in this context?
questions.e: To qualify as a biodiversity hotspot, a region must meet strict criteria: it must contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics (Endemism) and must have lost at least 70 percent of its original habitat (Threat perception). Species richness is the third core criterion.

questions.q: The Himalayan range is very rich in species diversity. Which one among the following is the most appropriate reason for this phenomenon? [2011-I]
o: (c) Exotic and invasive species have not been introduced in this region.
(b) It is a confluence of different bio-geographical zones.
(a) It has a high rainfall that supports luxuriant vegetative growth
questions.e: The Himalayas and their adjoining areas are marked as a confluence of several biogeographical realms, making the region rich in a variety of forest types and zoo-biogeographic diversity.

questions.q: There is a concern over the increase in harmful algal blooms in the seawaters of India. What could be the causative factors for this phenomenon? [2011-I] 1️⃣ Discharge of nutrients from the estuaries. 2️⃣ Run-off from the land during the monsoon. 3️⃣ Upwelling in the seas.
questions.e: Algae multiply rapidly when nutrients are present. Nutrient discharge from estuaries, land run-off during monsoons (carrying salts), and sea upwelling (bringing nutrients to the surface) all favor the growth of algal blooms.

questions.q: Consider the following: [2011-I] 1️⃣ Photosynthesis 2️⃣ Respiration 3️⃣ Decay of organic matter 4️⃣ Volcanic action. Which of the above add carbon dioxide to the carbon cycle on earth?
questions.e: Respiration, the decay of organic matter, and volcanic eruptions all release carbon dioxide into the atmosphere. Photosynthesis, conversely, removes carbon dioxide from the air to produce food.

questions.q: A sandy and saline area is the natural habitat of an Indian animal species. The animal has no predators in that area but its existence is threatened due to the destruction of its habitat. Which one of the following could be that animal? [2011-I]
questions.e: The Indian wild ass (also called ghudkhur) is native to saline desert areas. While they don't have natural predators, their numbers have declined due to habitat issues and diseases.

questions.q: Biodiversity forms the basis for human existence in the following ways: [2011-I] 1️⃣ Soil formation 2️⃣ Prevention of soil erosion 3️⃣ Recycling of waste 4️⃣ Pollination of crops. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.e: Biological diversity is essential for the formation and maintenance of soil structure, moisture retention, and nutrient levels. It also supports air quality, waste recycling, pollination, and prevents erosion.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a site for in-situ method of conservation of flora? [2011-I]
questions.e: Botanical gardens and zoos are methods of ex-situ conservation (outside the natural habitat). Biosphere Reserves, National Parks, and Wildlife Sanctuaries are examples of in-situ conservation (within the natural habitat).

questions.q: The 2004 Tsunami made people realize that mangroves can serve as a reliable safety hedge against coastal calamities. How do mangroves function as a safety hedge? [2011-I]
o: (b) The mangroves provide both food and medicines...
(c) The mangrove trees are tall with dense canopie...
(a) The mangrove swamps separate the human settlem...
(d) The mangrove trees do not get uprooted by stor...
questions.e: Mangrove trees have extensive root systems that prevent them from being uprooted by storms and tides, allowing them to act as a physical buffer or safety hedge for coastal areas.

questions.q: The "Red Data Books" published by the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural resources (IUCN) contain lists of? [2011-I] 1️⃣ Endemic plant and animal species present in the biodiversity hotspots. 2️⃣ Threatened plant and animal species. 3️⃣ Protected sites for conservation of nature and natural resources in various countries. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.e: The Red Data Books specifically contain lists of threatened plant and animal species. They do not primarily focus on hotspots or general protected sites in this context.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2011-I] 1️⃣ Biodiversity is normally greater in the lower latitudes as compared to the higher latitudes. 2️⃣ Along the mountain gradients, biodiversity is normally greater in the lower altitudes as compared to the higher altitudes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Biodiversity is higher in lower latitudes because habitat tolerance is narrower at higher latitudes. Similarly, lower altitudes on mountains can support a larger number of species due to more favorable climatic conditions.

questions.q: With reference to India, consider the following Central Acts: [2011-I] 1️⃣ Mining and Mineral Development (Regulation) Act, 1957 2️⃣ Customs Act, 1962 3️⃣ Import and Export (Control) Act, 1947 4️⃣ Indian Forest Act, 1927. Which of the above Acts have relevance to/bearing on the biodiversity conservation in the country?
questions.e: There are approximately 35 acts in India that have relevance to biodiversity conservation, including all those listed: mining regulation, customs, trade control, and forest management.

questions.q: Consider the following: [2011-I] 1️⃣ Carbon dioxide 2️⃣ Oxides of Nitrogen 3️⃣ Oxides of Sulphur. Which of the above is/are the emission/emissions from coal combustion at thermal power plants?
questions.e: The combustion of coal at thermal power plants releases several pollutants, including carbon dioxide (CO2), nitrogen oxides (NOx), and sulphur oxides (SOx).

questions.q: How does National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) help in protecting the Indian agriculture? [2012-I] 1️⃣ NBA checks the biopiracy and protects the indigenous and traditional genetic resources. 2️⃣ NBA directly monitors and supervises the scientific research on genetic modification of crop plants. 3️⃣ Application for Intellectual Property Rights related to genetic/biological resources cannot be made without the approval of NBA. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The NBA is responsible for checking biopiracy and protecting traditional genetic resources. Approval from the NBA is mandatory before applying for Intellectual Property Rights related to biological resources. It does not directly supervise research on genetic modification.

questions.q: The National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 was enacted in consonance with which of the following provisions of the Constitution of India? [2012-I] 1️⃣ Right to healthy environment, construed as a part of Right to life under Article 21 2️⃣ Provision of grants for raising the level of administration in the Scheduled Areas for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes under Article 275(1) 3️⃣ Powers and functions of Gram Sabha as mentioned under Article 243 (A). Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.e: The National Green Tribunal Act was enacted to uphold the right to a healthy environment, which is considered a component of the Right to Life under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: If National Water Mission is properly and completely implemented, how will it impact the country? [2012-I] 1️⃣ Part of the water needs of urban areas will be met through recycling of wastewater. 2️⃣ The water requirements of coastal cities with inadequate alternative sources of water will be met by adopting appropriate technologies that allow for the use of ocean water. 3️⃣ All the rivers of Himalayan origin will be linked to the rivers of peninsular India. 4️⃣ The expenses incurred by farmers for digging bore-wells and for installing motors and pump-sets to draw groundwater will be completely reimbursed by the Government. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.e: Implementation of the National Water Mission aims to meet urban water needs through recycling and provide water to coastal cities by using desalination technologies for ocean water. It does not mandate linking all rivers or full reimbursement for private wells.

questions.q: Biomass gasification is considered to be one of the sustainable solutions to the power crisis in India. In this context, which of the following statements is/are correct? [2012-I] 1️⃣ Coconut shells, groundnut shells and rice husk can be used in biomass gasification. 2️⃣ The combustible gases generated from biomass gasification consist of hydrogen and carbon dioxide only. 3️⃣ The combustible gases generated from biomass gasification can be used for direct heat generation but not in internal combustion engines.
questions.e: Various agricultural residues like coconut shells and rice husks can be used. However, the produced gases include carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide, and methane. These gases can indeed be used in internal combustion engines.

questions.q: The acidification of oceans is increasing. Why is this phenomenon a cause of concern? [2012-I] 1️⃣ The growth and survival of calcareous phytoplankton will be adversely affected. 2️⃣ The growth and survival of coral reefs will be adversely affected. 3️⃣ The survival of some animals that have phytoplanktonic larvae will be adversely affected. 4️⃣ The cloud seeding and formation of clouds will be adversely affected. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Ocean acidification adversely affects corals and phytoplankton, reducing their growth and survival. It also impacts animals with planktonic larvae and can lead to reduced cloud formation because acidified oceans produce less dimethylsulfide (DMS), which seeds clouds.

questions.q: The increasing amount of carbon dioxide in the air is slowly raising the temperature of the atmosphere, because it absorbs [2012-I]
o: (a) the water vapour of the air and retains its heat
(b) the ultraviolet part of the solar radiation
(d) the infrared part of the solar radiation
questions.e: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas that contributes to atmospheric warming by absorbing the infrared part of solar radiation.

questions.q: Consider the following protected areas: [2012-I] 1️⃣ Bandipur 2️⃣ Bhitarkanika 3️⃣ Manas 4️⃣ Sunderbans. Which of the above are declared Tiger Reserves?
questions.e: Bandipur, Manas, and Sunderbans are officially declared Tiger Reserves. Bhitarkanika is a National Park well-known for crocodiles, but it is not a Tiger Reserve.

questions.q: In which one among the following categories of protected areas in India are local people not allowed to collect and use the biomass? [2012-I]
questions.e: In National Parks, the collection and use of biomass by local people is strictly prohibited. This is a key difference between National Parks and other protected areas like Wildlife Sanctuaries.

questions.q: Which one of the following groups of animals belongs to the category of endangered species? [2012-I]
o: (c) Snow Leopard, Swamp Deer, Rhesus Monkey and Saras (Crane)
(a) Great Indian Bustard, Musk Deer, Red Panda and Asiatic Wild Ass
(b) Kashmir Stag, Cheetal, Blue Bull and Great Indian Bustard
(d) Lion-tailed Macaque, Blue Bull, Hanuman Langur and Cheetal
questions.e: The Great Indian Bustard, Musk Deer, Red Panda, and Asiatic Wild Ass are all classified as endangered species.

questions.q: The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment describes the following major categories of ecosystem services provisioning, supporting, regulating, preserving and cultural. Which one of the following is supporting service? [2012-I]
questions.e: Supporting services are those necessary for the production of all other ecosystem services; examples include soil formation, nutrient cycling, and photosynthesis.

questions.q: What is the difference between the antelopes Oryx and Chiru? [2012-I]
o: (d) None of the statements (a), (b) and (c) given...
(c) Oryx exists in western India only whereas Chir...
(a) Oryx is adapted to live in hot and arid areas...
(b) Oryx is poached for its antlers whereas Chiru...
questions.e: Oryx is adapted to hot and arid environments, while Chiru (Tibetan antelope) is adapted to the cold high-mountain steppes.

questions.q: Which of the following can be threats to the biodiversity of a geographical area? [2012-I] 1️⃣ Global warming 2️⃣ Fragmentation of habitat 3️⃣ Invasion of alien species 4️⃣ Promotion of vegetarianism.
questions.e: Global warming, habitat fragmentation, and invasive species are all recognized threats to biodiversity. Promotion of vegetarianism is not considered a threat to biodiversity.

questions.q: Consider the following agricultural practices: [2012-I] 1️⃣ Contour bunding 2️⃣ Relay cropping 3️⃣ Zero tillage. In the context of global climate change, which of the above helps/help in carbon sequestration/storage in the soil?
questions.e: Practices such as contour bunding, relay cropping, and zero tillage all contribute to carbon sequestration or storage within the soil, helping to mitigate climate change.

questions.q: What would happen if phytoplankton of an ocean is completely destroyed for some reason? [2012-I] 1️⃣ The ocean as a carbon sink would be adversely affected. 2️⃣ The food chains in the ocean would be adversely affected. 3️⃣ The density of ocean water would drastically decrease.
questions.e: Phytoplankton act as a primary carbon sink and form the base of marine food chains. Their destruction would severely impact these two functions, though it wouldn't drastically change the water density.

questions.q: Vultures which used to be very common in Indian countryside some years ago are rarely seen nowadays. This is attributed to [2012-I]
o: (b) a drug used by cattle owners for treating their diseased cattle
(c) scarcity of food available to them
(a) the destruction of their nesting sites by new invasive species
(d) a widespread, persistent and fatal disease among them
questions.e: The decline of vultures in India is primarily attributed to a specific drug (Diclofenac) used by cattle owners to treat diseased cattle, which is toxic to vultures when they scavenge on the carcasses.

questions.q: Due to improper/ indiscriminate disposal of old and used computers or their parts, which of the following are released into the environment as e-waste? [2013-I] 1️⃣ Beryllium 2️⃣ Cadmium 3️⃣ Chromium 4️⃣ Heptachlor 5️⃣ Mercury 6️⃣ Lead 7️⃣ Plutonium.
questions.e: E-waste contains various hazardous elements including lead, mercury, cadmium, and hexavalent chromium. Heptachlor is a pesticide and Plutonium is a radioactive element not typically found in standard computer e-waste.

questions.q: With reference to food chains in ecosystems, consider the following statements: [2013-I] 1️⃣ A food chain illustrates the order in which a chain of organisms feed upon each other. 2️⃣ Food chains are found within the populations of a species. 3️⃣ A food chain illustrates the numbers of each organism which are eaten by others. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A food chain is a sequence of "who eats whom" in a biological community to obtain nutrition. It illustrates the flow of energy between different species, not within a single species population, and it doesn't primarily illustrate the absolute numbers.

questions.q: In which of the following States is lion-tailed macaque found in its natural habitat? [2013-I] 1️⃣ Tamil Nadu 2️⃣ Kerala 3️⃣ Karnataka 4️⃣ Andhra Pradesh.
questions.e: Lion-tailed macaques are endangered primates found in the mountain forests of the Western Ghats, specifically scattered across the states of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka.

questions.q: Which one of the following terms describes not only the physical space occupied by an organism, but also its functional role in the community of organisms? [2013-I]
questions.e: An ecological niche describes the way of life of a species, including how it responds to the distribution of resources and competitors—effectively its functional role and habitat requirements.

questions.q: Consider the following: [2013-I] 1️⃣ Star tortoise 2️⃣ Monitor lizard 3️⃣ Pygmy hog 4️⃣ Spider monkey. Which of the above are naturally found in India?
questions.e: Star tortoises, monitor lizards, and pygmy hogs (found in Assam) are native to India. Spider monkeys are inhabitants of the tropical forests of Central and South America.

questions.q: Which of the following can be found as pollutants in the drinking water in some parts of India? [2013-I] 1️⃣ Arsenic 2️⃣ Sorbitol 3️⃣ Fluoride 4️⃣ Formaldehyde 5️⃣ Uranium.
questions.e: Arsenic (from orchard run-off) and Fluoride (from natural deposits and factories) are well-known drinking water contaminants in parts of India. Uranium has also been found as a pollutant in certain regions.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: [2013-I] 1️⃣ Nokrek Biosphere Reserve : Garo Hills 2️⃣ Logtak (Loktak) Lake : Barail Range 3️⃣ Namdapha National Park : Dafla Hills. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Nokrek is indeed in the Garo Hills (Meghalaya). However, Loktak Lake is in Manipur (not Barail Range), and while Namdapha and Dafla Hills are both in Arunachal Pradesh, they are separate entities.

questions.q: In the grasslands, trees do not replace the grasses as a part of an ecological succession because of [2013-I]
o: (b) limited sunlight and paucity of nutrients
questions.e: In grassland ecosystems, factors like seasonal rainfall/water availability and frequent fires prevent trees from establishing themselves and replacing the grasses during succession.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of ecosystems in the order of decreasing productivity? [2013-I]
questions.e: The correct order of decreasing productivity among these ecosystems is: Mangroves > Grasslands > Lakes > Oceans.

questions.q: Consider the following fauna of India: [2013-I] 1️⃣ Gharial 2️⃣ Leatherback turtle 3️⃣ Swamp deer. Which of the above is/are endangered?
questions.e: Gharials are critically endangered due to habitat loss and hunting. Leatherback turtles and swamp deer are also classified as endangered species due to various human activities and habitat destruction.

questions.q: With reference to the food chains in ecosystems, which of the following kinds of organism is/are known as decomposer organism/organisms? [2013-I] 1️⃣ Virus 2️⃣ Fungi 3️⃣ Bacteria.
questions.e: Bacteria and fungi are primary decomposers that break down organic matter. Viruses are not decomposers; they are intracellular parasites.

questions.q: Consider the following international agreements: [2014-I] 1️⃣ The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture 2️⃣ The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification 3️⃣ The World Heritage Convention. Which of the above has/have a bearing on the biodiversity?
questions.e: All three agreements impact biodiversity: the first via crop genetic resource conservation, the second by addressing land degradation, and the third through the protection of natural heritage sites.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding 'Earth Hour': [2014-I] 1️⃣ It is an initiative of UNEP and UNESCO. 2️⃣ It is a movement in which the participants switch off the lights for one hour on a certain day every year. 3️⃣ It is a movement to raise the awareness about the climate change and the need to save the planet. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Earth Hour is organized by the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), not UNEP/UNESCO. It involves switching off non-essential lights for one hour to raise awareness about climate change.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of a food chain? [2014-I]
questions.e: In this marine food chain, Diatoms (autotrophs/producers) are eaten by Crustaceans (herbivorous primary consumers), which are then eaten by Herrings (carnivorous secondary consumers).

questions.q: If a wetland of international importance is brought under the 'Montreux Record', what does it imply? [2014-I]
o: (d) It is given the status of 'World Heritage Site...
(c) The survival of the wetland depends on the cul...
(a) Changes in ecological character have occurred,...
(b) The country in which the wetland is located sh...
questions.e: The Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar sites where ecological changes have occurred or are likely to occur due to human interference such as pollution or technological development.

questions.q: With reference to Bombay Natural History Society (BNHS), consider the following statements: [2014-I] 1️⃣ It is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Environment and Forests. 2️⃣ It strives to conserve nature through action-based research, education and public awareness. 3️⃣ It organizes and conducts nature trails and camps for the general public. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: BNHS is a large non-governmental organization, not a government body. It is dedicated to conservation and biodiversity research through education, awareness, and public nature camps.

questions.q: With reference to 'Global Environment Facility', which of the following statements is/are correct? [2014-I]
o: (b) It undertakes scientific research on environme...
(c) It is an agency under OECD to facilitate the t...
(a) It serves as financial mechanism for 'Conventi...
questions.e: The GEF is an independent financial organization that serves as a financial mechanism for several international environmental conventions, including the CBD and UNFCCC.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: [2014-I] 1️⃣ Dampa Tiger Reserve : Mizoram 2️⃣ Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary : Sikkim 3️⃣ Saramati Peak : Nagaland. Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Dampa Tiger Reserve is in Mizoram and Saramati Peak is in Nagaland. Gumti Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Tripura, not Sikkim.

questions.q: With reference to a conservation organization called "Wetlands International', which of the following statements is/are correct? [2014-I] 1️⃣ It is an intergovernmental organization formed by the countries which are signatories to Ramsar Convention. 2️⃣ It works at the field level to develop and mobilize knowledge, and use the practical experience to advocate for better policies. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Wetlands International is a partnership organization, not an intergovernmental one formed by Ramsar. It was formed in 1954, predating the 1971 Ramsar Convention. It works to mobilize knowledge for better wetland policies.

questions.q: Other than poaching, what are the possible reasons for the decline in the population of Ganges River Dolphins? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Construction of dams and barrages on rivers 2️⃣ Increase in the population of crocodiles in rivers 3️⃣ Getting trapped in fishing nets accidentally 4️⃣ Use of synthetic fertilizers and other agricultural chemicals in crop-fields in the vicinity of rivers.
questions.e: The decline of Ganges river dolphins is caused by dams, accidental entanglement in nets, and chemical pollution from agriculture. Increasing crocodile populations is not a noted reason for their decline.

questions.q: Which of the following adds/add carbon dioxide to the carbon cycle on the planet Earth? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Volcanic action 2️⃣ Respiration 3️⃣ Photosynthesis 4️⃣ Decay of organic matter.
questions.e: Volcanic action, respiration, and the decay of organic matter add CO2 to the cycle. Photosynthesis is the process that removes CO2 from the cycle.

questions.q: If you walk through countryside, you are likely to see some birds stalking alongside the cattle to seize the insects disturbed by their movement through grasses. Which of the following is/are such bird/birds? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Painted Stork 2️⃣ Common Myna 3️⃣ Black-necked Crane.
questions.e: The Common Myna is known to stalk alongside cattle to eat insects flushed out by the cattle's movement.

questions.q: With reference to 'Eco-Sensitive Zones', which of the following statements is/are correct? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Eco-Sensitive Zones are the areas that are declared under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. 2️⃣ The purpose of the declaration of Eco-Sensitive Zones is to prohibit all kinds of human activities in those zones except agriculture. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Eco-sensitive zones are declared under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (not the 1972 Act). Their purpose is to regulate, not prohibit, certain human activities around protected areas.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2014-I] 1️⃣ Animal Welfare Board of India is established under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. 2️⃣ National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body. 3️⃣ National Ganga River Basin Authority is chaired by the Prime Minister. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Animal Welfare Board was established under the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. The NTCA is a statutory body, and the Prime Minister chairs the NGRBA.

questions.q: Which of the following have coral reefs? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Andaman and Nicobar Islands 2️⃣ Gulf of Kachchh 3️⃣ Gulf of Mannar 4️⃣ Sunderbans.
questions.e: Coral reefs in India are found in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Gulf of Kachchh, and the Gulf of Mannar. The Sunderbans do not have coral reefs.

questions.q: In India, the problem of soil erosion is associated with which of the following? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Terrace cultivation 2️⃣ Deforestation 3️⃣ Tropical climate.
questions.e: Soil erosion in India is heavily associated with deforestation. Terrace cultivation is actually a practice used to prevent soil erosion.

questions.q: The most important strategy for the conservation of biodiversity together with traditional human life is the establishment of [2014-I]
questions.e: Biosphere reserves, established under UNESCO's MAB programme, are unique because they combine protected areas with zones where traditional native life and sustainable development are nurtured.

questions.q: If the global temperature increases beyond $3^{\circ}C$ above the pre-industrial level, what can be its possible impact/impacts on the world? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Terrestrial biosphere tends toward a net carbon source. 2️⃣ Widespread coral mortality will occur. 3️⃣ All the global wetlands will permanently disappear. 4️⃣ Cultivation of cereals will not be possible anywhere in the world.
questions.e: A $3^{\circ}C$ rise would likely turn the terrestrial biosphere into a net carbon source and cause widespread coral death. It would not cause the total disappearance of all wetlands or make global cereal cultivation impossible.

questions.q: Lichens, which are capable of initiating ecological succession even on a bare rock, are actually a symbiotic association of [2014-I]
questions.e: Lichens are a symbiotic relationship between an alga (which provides food through photosynthesis) and a fungus (which provides shelter, water, and minerals).

questions.q: Which of the following are some important pollutants released by steel industry in India? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Oxides of sulphur 2️⃣ Oxides of nitrogen 3️⃣ Carbon monoxide 4️⃣ Carbon dioxide.
questions.e: Steel furnace operations involve coke reacting with iron, which releases pollutants including oxides of sulphur and nitrogen, carbon monoxide, and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Every year, a monthlong ecologically important campaign/ festival is held during which certain communities/tribes plant saplings of fruit-bearing trees. Which of the following are such communities/tribes? [2014-I]
questions.e: The festival celebrated by planting fruit-bearing saplings on a mass scale is associated with the Gond and Korku tribes.

questions.q: In India, cluster bean (Guar) is traditionally used as a vegetable or animal feed, but recently the cultivation of this has assumed significance. Which one of the following statements is correct in this context? [2014-I]
o: (b) The gum made from its seeds is used in the extraction of shale gas
(d) It is a source of high quality biodiesel
(c) The leaf extract of this plant has the properties of antihistamines
(a) The oil extracted from seeds is used in the manufacture of biodegradable plastics
questions.e: While traditionally used as food or feed, the gum extracted from cluster bean (Guar) seeds has recently become vital for the extraction of shale gas.

questions.q: If you travel through the Himalayas, you are likely to see which of the following plants naturally growing there? [2014-I] 1️⃣ Oak 2️⃣ Rhododendron 3️⃣ Sandalwood.
questions.e: Oak and Rhododendron are native plants of the Himalayan zone. Sandalwood is naturally found in South India, not the Himalayas.

questions.q: Which one of the following National Parks has a climate that varies from tropical to subtropical, temperate and arctic? [2015-I]
questions.e: Namdapha National Park in Arunachal Pradesh has a diverse climate that ranges from tropical/subtropical in the southern regions to arctic in its northern parts.

questions.q: 'BioCarbon Fund Initiative for Sustainable Forest Landscapes' is managed by the [2015-I]
questions.e: The BioCarbon Fund is a public-private initiative housed within the Carbon Finance Unit of the World Bank to support carbon sequestration in forest and agro-ecosystems.

questions.q: With reference to 'Forest Carbon Partnership Facility', which of the following statements is/ are correct? [2015-I] 1️⃣ It is a global partnership of governments, businesses, civil society and indigenous peoples. 2️⃣ It provides financial aid to universities, individual scientists and institutions involved in scientific forestry research. 3️⃣ It assists the countries in their 'REDD+' efforts by providing them with financial and technical assistance.
questions.e: The FCPF is a global partnership focused on helping developing countries with REDD+ efforts through financial and technical aid. It does not primarily exist to provide scientific research grants to individual scientists.

questions.q: With reference to an organization known as 'Birdlife International', which of the following statements is/are correct? [2015-I] 1️⃣ It is a Global Partnership of Conservation Organizations. 2️⃣ The concept of 'biodiversity hotspots' originated from this organization. 3️⃣ It identifies the sites known/referred to as 'Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas'.
questions.e: BirdLife International is the world's largest conservation partnership and identifies Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas (IBAs). The concept of biodiversity hotspots did not originate from this organization.

questions.q: In India, in which one of the following types of forests is teak a dominant tree species? [2015-I]
questions.e: Teak (along with Sal) is a dominant tree species found in Tropical Moist Deciduous forests, which occur in the Sahyadris, north-eastern peninsula, and Himalayan foothills.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the best description of the term 'ecosystem'? [2015-I]
o: (d) The flora and fauna of a geographical area
(a) A community of organisms interacting with one another.
(b) That part of the Earth which is inhabited by living organisms.
(c) A community of organisms together with the environment in which they live
questions.e: An ecosystem encompasses all living organisms (plants, animals) in a specific area interacting with each other and their non-living environment (weather, soil, atmosphere).

questions.q: Which of the following National Parks is unique in being a swamp with floating vegetation that supports a rich biodiversity? [2015-I]
questions.e: Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur is the only floating park in the world, consisting of a swamp with floating vegetation (phumdis).

questions.q: With reference to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) and the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES), which of the following statements is/are correct? [2015-I] 1️⃣ IUCN is an organ of the United Nations and CITES is an international agreement between governments. 2️⃣ IUCN runs thousands of field projects around the world to better manage natural environments. 3️⃣ CITES is legally binding on the States that have joined it, but this Convention does not take the place of national laws.
questions.e: IUCN is not an organ of the UN (though it has observer status). IUCN runs many field projects, and while CITES is legally binding on parties, it does not replace their national laws.

questions.q: With reference to 'dugong', a mammal found in India, which of the following statements is/are correct? [2015-I] 1️⃣ It is a herbivorous marine animal. 2️⃣ It is found along the entire coast of India. 3️⃣ It is given legal protection under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
questions.e: The dugong is a herbivorous marine mammal given the highest level of protection under Schedule I of the 1972 Act. It is not found along the entire coast of India.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the national aquatic animal of India? [2015-I]
questions.e: The Gangetic River Dolphin was notified as the National Aquatic Animal of India in May 2010.

questions.q: Which one of the following is associated with the issue of control and phasing out of the use of ozone-depleting substances? [2015-I]
questions.e: The Montreal Protocol is the international treaty specifically designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out substances like CFCs that cause ozone depletion.

questions.q: What is Rio+20 Conference, often mentioned in the news? [2015-I]
o: (d) It is a Conference of the Member Countries of the Convention on Biological Diversity
(c) It is a Conference of the Inter-governmental Panel on Climate Change
(a) It is the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development
(b) It is a Ministerial Meeting of the World Trade Organization
questions.e: Rio+20 is the common name for the United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development held in Rio de Janeiro in 2012, twenty years after the original 1992 Earth Summit.

questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding 'Green Climate Fund' is/are correct? [2015-I] 1️⃣ It is intended to assist the developing countries in adaptation and mitigation practices to counter climate change. 2️⃣ It is founded under the aegis of UNEP, OECD, Asian Development Bank and World Bank.
questions.e: The Green Climate Fund is a mechanism within the UNFCCC to redistribute funds from developed to developing countries for climate adaptation and mitigation. It was not founded by the specific group of organizations listed in statement 2.

questions.q: With reference to bio-toilets used by the Indian Railways, consider the following statements: [2015-I] 1️⃣ The decomposition of human waste in the bio-toilets is initiated by a fungal inoculum. 2️⃣ Ammonia and water vapour are the only end products in this decomposition which are released into the atmosphere.
questions.e: Bio-toilets use a bacterial (not fungal) inoculum to decompose waste into carbon dioxide, methane, and neutral water.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: Terms — Their origin [2016-I] 1️⃣ Annex-I Countries : Cartagena Protocol 2️⃣ Certified Emissions Reductions : Nagoya Protocol 3️⃣ Clean Development Mechanism : Kyoto Protocol. Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.e: Annex-I Countries, Certified Emissions Reductions (CERs), and the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) are all terms originating from or associated with the Kyoto Protocol.

questions.q: With reference to an initiative called 'The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB)', which of the following statements is/are correct? [2016-I] 1️⃣ It is an initiative hosted by UNEP, IMF and World Economic Forum. 2️⃣ It is a global initiative that focuses on drawing attention to the economic benefits of biodiversity. 3️⃣ It presents an approach that can help decision-makers recognize, demonstrate and capture the value of ecosystems and biodiversity.
questions.e: TEEB is an international initiative to highlight the economic benefits of biodiversity and provide a framework for decision-makers. It is not hosted by the IMF or World Economic Forum.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? Proper design and effective implementation of UN-REDD+ Programme can significantly contribute to [2016-I] 1️⃣ protection of biodiversity 2️⃣ resilience of forest ecosystems 3️⃣ poverty reduction.
questions.e: According to official guidelines (and as confirmed by UPSC), the REDD+ programme contributes to biodiversity protection, forest resilience, and indirectly to poverty reduction.

questions.q: What is 'Greenhouse Gas Protocol'? [2016-I]
o: (d) It is one of the multilateral REDD+ initiative...
(a) It is an international accounting tool for gov...
(b) It is an initiative of the United Nations to o...
(c) It is an inter-governmental agreement ratified...
questions.e: The GHG Protocol is a widely used international accounting tool created by a partnership between the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD).

questions.q: With reference to 'Agenda 21', sometimes seen in the news, consider the following statements: [2016-I] 1️⃣ It is a global action plan for sustainable development. 2️⃣ It originated in the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in Johannesburg in 2002.
questions.e: Agenda 21 is a non-binding action plan for sustainable development that originated at the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro, not the 2002 Johannesburg summit.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2016-I] 1️⃣ The International Solar Alliance was launched at the United Nations Climate Change Conference in 2015. 2️⃣ The Alliance includes all the member countries of the United Nations.
questions.e: The ISA was launched at COP-21 in Paris (2015). However, it specifically includes an alliance of countries located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, not all UN member countries.

questions.q: With reference to the Agreement at the UNFCCC Meeting in Paris in 2015, which of the following statements is/are correct? [2016-I] 1️⃣ The Agreement was signed by all the member countries of the UN and it will go into effect in 2017. 2️⃣ The Agreement aims to limit the greenhouse gas emissions so that the rise in average global temperature by the end of this century does not exceed $2^{\circ}C$ or even $1.5^{\circ}C$ above pre-industrial levels. 3️⃣ Developed countries committed to donate $ 1000 billion a year from 2020 to help developing countries to cope with climate change.
questions.e: The Paris Agreement aims to hold global temperature increases well below $2^{\circ}C$. Not all UN nations signed it immediately, and the financial commitment from developed countries was $100 billion per year, not $1000 billion.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2016-I] 1️⃣ The Sustainable Development Goals were first proposed in 1972 by a global think tank called the 'Club of Rome'. 2️⃣ The Sustainable Development Goals have to be achieved by 2030. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The SDGs were adopted in 2015 and have a target date of 2030. While the Club of Rome is a think tank that deals with political issues, it did not propose the current SDGs in 1972.

questions.q: The term 'Intended Nationally Determined Contributions' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of [2016-I]
o: (b) plan of action outlined by the countries of th...
(a) pledges made by the European countries to reha...
(c) capital contributed by the member countries in...
(d) plan of action outlined by the countries of th...
questions.e: INDCs are climate change commitments made by individual countries under the UNFCCC framework leading up to the 2015 Paris Agreement.

questions.q: What is/are the importance/importances of the 'United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification'? [2016-I] 1️⃣ It aims to promote effective action through innovative national programs and supportive inter-national partnerships. 2️⃣ It has a special/particular focus on South Asia and North Africa regions, and its Secretariat facilitates the allocation of major portion of financial resources to these regions. 3️⃣ It is committed to bottom-up approach, encouraging the participation of local people in combating the desertification.
questions.e: The UNCCD promotes national programs and a bottom-up approach involving local people. It focuses on several global regions including Africa, Asia, and Latin America, not just South Asia and North Africa.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes/ describe the aim of 'Green India Mission' of the Government of India? [2016-I] 1️⃣ Incorporating environmental benefits and costs into the Union and State Budgets thereby implementing the green accounting. 2️⃣ Launching the second green revolution to enhance agricultural output. 3️⃣ Restoring and enhancing forest cover and responding to climate change by a combination of adaptation and mitigation measures.
questions.e: The Green India Mission aims to increase forest and tree cover and improve the quality of existing forest cover as part of climate change adaptation and mitigation. It is not primarily about green accounting or a second green revolution.

questions.q: 'Net metering' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of promoting the [2016-I]
o: (c) installation of CNG kits in motor-cars
(b) use of piped natural gas in the kitchens of households
(d) installation of water meters in urban households
(a) production and use of solar energy by the households/consumers
questions.e: Net metering is a billing mechanism that allows residential or commercial customers who generate their own solar or wind power to feed unused electricity back into the grid for credit.

questions.q: 'Gadgil Committee Report' and 'Kasturirangan Committee Report', sometimes seen in the news, are related to [2016-I]
questions.e: Both the Gadgil and Kasturirangan reports were focused on environmental protection and sustainable development plans specifically for the Western Ghats.

questions.q: On which of the following can you find the Bureau of Energy Efficiency Star Label? [2016-I] 1️⃣ Ceiling fans 2️⃣ Electric geysers 3️⃣ Tubular fluorescent lamps.
questions.e: The BEE star label, which indicates energy efficiency, is mandatory or available for a wide range of appliances in India, including ceiling fans, geysers, and fluorescent lamps.

questions.q: In the cities of our country, which among the following atmospheric gases are normally considered in calculating the value of Air Quality Index? [2016-I] 1️⃣ Carbon dioxide 2️⃣ Carbon monoxide 3️⃣ Nitrogen dioxide 4️⃣ Sulfur dioxide 5️⃣ Methane.
questions.e: The Air Quality Index (AQI) is based on 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb. Carbon dioxide and methane are not part of the AQI calculation.

questions.q: Which of the following are the key features of 'National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA)'? [2016-I] 1️⃣ River basin is the unit of planning and management. 2️⃣ It spearheads the river conservation efforts at the national level. 3️⃣ One of the Chief Ministers of the States through which the Ganga flows becomes the Chairman of NGRBA on rotation basis.
questions.e: NGRBA uses the river basin as the management unit and leads national conservation efforts. However, it is chaired by the Prime Minister, not a rotating Chief Minister.

questions.q: What is/are unique about 'Kharai camel', a breed found in India? [2016-I] 1️⃣ It is capable of swimming up to three kilometers in seawater. 2️⃣ It survives by grazing on mangroves. 3️⃣ It lives in the wild and cannot be domesticated.
questions.e: Kharai camels in Kutch are unique because they can swim and feed on mangroves. They are domesticated by the Jatt and Rabari communities and are not strictly wild.

questions.q: Recently, our scientists have discovered a new and distinct species of banana plant which attains a height of about 11 metres and has orange-coloured fruit pulp. In which part of India has it been discovered? [2016-I]
questions.e: This new 11-meter tall species of banana with orange pulp was discovered by the Botanical Survey of India in the rain forests of the Little Andaman islands.

questions.q: With reference to 'Red Sanders', sometimes seen in the news, consider the following statements: [2016-I] 1️⃣ It is a tree species found in a part of South India. 2️⃣ It is one of the most important trees in the tropical rain forest areas of South India.
questions.e: Red Sanders is endemic to the Eastern Ghats of South India. However, it is a species associated with tropical dry deciduous forests, not tropical rain forests.

questions.q: The term 'M-STRPES' is sometimes seen in the news in the context of [2017-I]
questions.e: MSTrIPES is a computerized tiger monitoring and patrolling protocol implemented by the National Tiger Conservation Authority in tiger reserves.

questions.q: Recently there was a proposal to translocate some of the lions from their natural habitat in Gujarat to which one of the following sites ? [2017-I]
questions.e: Kuno-Palpur Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh was the site chosen for the proposed translocation of Asiatic lions from Gujarat.

questions.q: In India, if a species of tortoise is declared protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, what does it imply? [2017-I]
o: (d) Both (b) and (c) stated above are correct in t...
(a) It enjoys the same level of protection as the...
(b) It no longer exists in the wild, a few individ...
(c) It is endemic to a particular region of India.
questions.e: Animals listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, such as the tiger, receive the highest level of legal protection in India.

questions.q: According to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, which of the following animals cannot be hunted by any person except under some provisions provided by law? [2017-I] 1️⃣ Gharial 2️⃣ Indian wild ass 3️⃣ Wild buffalo.
questions.e: Gharials, Indian wild asses, and wild buffaloes are protected under the Wildlife Protection Act and cannot be hunted. Only certain animals classified as "vermin" (like mice or crows) in Schedule 5 can be hunted.

questions.q: If you want to see gharials in their natural habitat, which one of the following is the best place to visit? [2017-I]
questions.e: The Chambal River Sanctuary holds the only viable population of gharials in their natural habitat.

questions.q: From the ecological point of view, which one of the following assumes importance in being a good link between the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats? [2017-I]
questions.e: The Eastern and Western Ghats meet at the Nilgiri hills. Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, located in this region in Tamil Nadu, serves as an important ecological link between the two mountain ranges.

questions.q: Consider the following statements in respect of Trade Related Analysis of Fauna and Flora in Commerce (TRAFFIC): [2017-I] 1️⃣ TRAFFIC is a bureau under United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). 2️⃣ The mission of TRAFFIC is to ensure that trade in wild plants and animals is not a threat to the conservation of nature. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.e: TRAFFIC is a joint program of the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) and IUCN, not a UNEP bureau. Its mission is to ensure wildlife trade does not threaten nature conservation.

questions.q: Due to some reasons, if there is a huge fall in the population of species of butterflies, what could be its likely consequence/consequences? [2017-I] 1️⃣ Pollination of some plants could be adversely affected. 2️⃣ There could be a drastic increase in the fungal infections of some cultivated plants. 3️⃣ It could lead to a fall in the population of some species of wasps, spiders and birds.
questions.e: A fall in butterfly population would affect pollination (as they are pollinators) and impact their predators, such as wasps, spiders, and birds. There is no established direct link between butterfly populations and "drastic" increases in fungal infections.

questions.q: Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a standard criterion for [2017-I]
o: (b) Computing oxygen levels in forest ecosystems
(d) Assessing oxygen levels in high altitude regions
questions.e: BOD is the amount of oxygen required by bacteria to break down organic matter in water. It is a standard measure of organic pollution in aquatic ecosystems.

questions.q: In the context of solving pollution problems, what is/are the advantage/advantages of bioremediation technique? [2017-I] 1️⃣ It is a technique for cleaning up pollution by enhancing the same biodegradation process that occurs in nature. 2️⃣ Any contaminant with heavy metals such as cadmium and lead can be readily and completely treated by bioremediation using micro-organisms. 3️⃣ Genetic engineering can be used to create microorganisms specifically designed for bioremediation.
questions.e: Bioremediation enhances natural biodegradation and can involve genetically engineered organisms. However, not all heavy metals can be "readily and completely" treated, as bioremediation often takes a long time and some compounds are resistant.

questions.q: In the context of mitigating the impending global warming due to anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide, which of the following can be the potential sites for carbon sequestration? [2017-I] 1️⃣ Abandoned and uneconomic coal seams 2️⃣ Depleted oil and gas reservoirs 3️⃣ Subterranean deep saline formations.
questions.e: Carbon sequestration can be done in artificial sinks such as unminable coal seams, depleted oil/gas reservoirs, and deep saline formations, which have a very high capacity for storage.

questions.q: It is possible to produce algae based biofuels, but what is/are the likely limitation(s) of developing countries in promoting this industry? [2017-I] 1️⃣ Production of algae based biofuels is possible in seas only and not on continents. 2️⃣ Setting up and engineering the algae based biofuel production requires high level of expertise/technology until the construction is completed. 3️⃣ Economically viable production necessitates the setting up of large scale facilities which may raise ecological and social concerns.
questions.e: Algae biofuel production faces technological challenges and requires large-scale facilities that can cause ecological and social concerns. It is not limited to seas and can be produced on land.

questions.q: With reference to 'Global Climate Change Alliance', which of the following statements is/are correct? [2017-I] 1️⃣ It is an initiative of the European Union. 2️⃣ It provides technical and financial support to targeted developing countries to integrate climate change into their development policies and budgets. 3️⃣ It is coordinated by World Resources Institute (WRI) and World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD).
questions.e: The GCCA is an initiative of the European Union to support developing countries with climate policies. It is overseen by the EU Commission, not by WRI or WBCSD.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2017-I] 1️⃣ Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC) to reduce Short Lived Climate Pollutants is a unique initiative of G20 group of countries. 2️⃣ The CCAC focuses on methane, black carbon and hydrofluorocarbons. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: CCAC was formed in 2012 by UNEP along with several countries (like Ghana and Bangladesh), not as a G20 initiative. It specifically focuses on short-lived pollutants like methane and black carbon.

questions.q: Why is a plant called Prosopis juliflora often mentioned in news? [2018-I]
o: (c) Its extract is used in the synthesis of pesticides.
(b) It tends to reduce the biodiversity in the area in which it grows.
(a) Its extract is widely used in cosmetics.
questions.e: Prosopis juliflora is an invasive alien species from Mexico. It is an aggressive colonizer that spreads through wastelands and forests, tending to reduce the local biodiversity.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes "carbon fertilization"? [2018-I]
o: (a) Increased plant growth due to increased concen...
(c) Increased acidity of oceans as a result of inc...
(d) Adaptation of all living beings on Earth to th...
(b) Increased temperature of Earth due to increase...
questions.e: Carbon fertilization refers to the phenomenon where increased atmospheric CO2 concentrations spur plant growth by increasing the rate of photosynthesis.

questions.q: The term "sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction" is often mentioned in the news in the context of the discussion of [2018-I]
o: (c) Large scale cultivation of genetically modifie...
(b) Fears of a possible collision of a meteorite w...
questions.e: Scientists suggest a sixth mass extinction is underway due to human-induced factors such as habitat loss, over-harvesting, pollution, and climate change, leading to high annual species loss.

questions.q: How is the National Green Tribunal (NGT) different from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)? [2018-I] 1️⃣ The NGT has been established by an Act whereas the CPCB has been created by an executive order of the Government. 2️⃣ The NGT provides environmental justice and helps reduce the burden of litigation in the higher courts whereas the CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells, and aims to improve the quality of air in the country.
questions.e: Both NGT and CPCB are statutory bodies established by Acts (NGT Act, 2010 and Water Act, 1974 respectively). NGT focuses on legal environmental justice, while CPCB is a technical body promoting environmental cleanliness.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2018-I] 1️⃣ The definition of "Critical Wildlife Habitat" is incorporated in the Forest Rights Act, 2006. 2️⃣ For the first time in India, Baigas have been given Habitat Rights. 3️⃣ Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change officially decides and declares Habitat Rights for Primitive and Vulnerable Tribal Groups in any part of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: "Critical Wildlife Habitat" is defined in the FRA, 2006. In 2016, the Baiga community became the first to receive habitat rights. Decision-making on rights happens at district-level committees, not directly by the Union Ministry.

questions.q: In which one of the following States is Pakhui Wildlife Sanctuary located? [2018-I]
questions.e: Pakhui (also known as Pakke) Wildlife Sanctuary and Tiger Reserve is located in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.q: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE), a UN mechanism to assist countries transition towards greener and more inclusive economies, emerged at [2018-I]
o: (c) The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change 2015, Paris
(b) The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development 2012, Rio de Janeiro
(a) The Earth Summit on Sustainable Development 2002, Johannesburg
(d) The World Sustainable Development Summit 2016, New Delhi
questions.e: PAGE was launched in 2013 as a direct response to the call for support for green economy transitions made at the Rio+20 conference in 2012.

questions.q: "Momentum for Change Climate Neutral Now" is an initiative launched by [2018-I]
o: (a) The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
questions.e: The UNFCCC Secretariat launched the Climate Neutral Now initiative in 2015 and later added it as a pillar under its Momentum for Change initiative.

questions.q: Which one of the following national parks lies completely in the Temperate alpine zone? [2019-I]
questions.e: Among the options provided, the Valley of Flowers National Park is the one that lies entirely within the temperate alpine climatic zone.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2019-I] 1️⃣ Asiatic lion naturally found in India only 2️⃣ Double-humped camel is naturally found in India only 3️⃣ One-horned rhinoceros is naturally found in India only. Which one of the statement given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Asiatic lions are naturally found only in India. Double-humped (Bactrian) camels are native to Central Asia, and the one-horned rhinoceros is found in other parts of Asia like Java (Indonesia).

questions.q: In the context of which of the following do some scientists suggest the use of cirrus cloud thinning technique and the injection of sulphate aerosol into stratosphere? [2019-I]
o: (a) Creating the artificial rains in some regions
(c) Reducing the adverse effects of the solar wind on the earth
(b) Reducing the frequency and intensity of tropical cyclones
questions.e: Scientists suggest stratospheric sulphate aerosol injection because these particles reflect sunlight, which could theoretically offset some of the temperature rise caused by global warming.

questions.q: Which one of the following are Agasthyamala biosphere reserve? [2019-I]
o: (d) Kawal and Shree Venkateshwara wildlife sanctuaries; and Nagarjunasagar-srisailam tiger reserve
(c) Kaundinya gundla bhrameshwaram and papikonda wildlife sanctuaries and mukurthi national park
(b) Mudumalai sathayamangalam and Wayanad wildlife sanctuaries and silent valley national park
(a) Neyyar, peppara and shendurney wildlife sanctuaries and kalakad mundanthurai tiger reserve
questions.e: The Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve includes the Neyyar, Peppara, and Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuaries along with the Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs: Wildlife — Naturally found in [2019-I] 1️⃣ Blue finned mahseer : Cauvery river 2️⃣ Irrawaddy dolphin : Chambal river 3️⃣ Rusty spotted cats : Eastern ghats. Which one of the pair given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Blue-finned mahseer is found in the Cauvery. Irrawaddy dolphins are found in Chilika lagoon and estuaries, while the Chambal river is home to the Gangetic river dolphin.

questions.q: Why is there a great concern about the microbeads that are released into environment? [2019-I]
o: (d) They are often found to be used as food adulterants
(a) They are considered harmful to marine ecosystem
(b) They are considered to cause skin cancer in children
(c) They are small enough to absorbed by crop plants in irrigated fields
questions.e: Microbeads in cosmetics have been classified as unsafe and dangerous for aquatic life because they are easily ingested by marine organisms and persist in the environment.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are correct about the deposits of methane hydrate? [2019-I] 1️⃣ Global warming might trigger the release of methane gas from these deposits 2️⃣ Large deposits of 'methane hydrate' are found in Arctic Tundra and under the seafloor. 3️⃣ Methane in atmosphere oxidizes to carbon dioxide after a decade or two.
questions.e: Methane hydrates are frozen in the Tundra and marine sediments; warming could release this methane. Once in the atmosphere, methane molecules remain for about a decade before oxidizing into CO2.

questions.q: Consider the following: [2019-I] 1️⃣ Carbon monoxide 2️⃣ Methane 3️⃣ Ozone 4️⃣ Sulphur dioxide. Which of the above are released into the atmosphere due to the burning of crop/biomass residue?
questions.e: Biomass burning releases greenhouse gases like CO2 and methane, as well as chemically active gases like carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide. These contribute to the production of tropospheric ozone.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2019-I] 1️⃣ Agricultural soils release nitrogen oxides into environment. 2️⃣ Cattle release ammonia into environment. 3️⃣ Poultry industry release reactive nitrogen compounds into environment. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: In India, agricultural soils contribute significantly to N2O emissions, cattle are responsible for the majority of ammonia production, and the poultry industry releases reactive nitrogen compounds.

questions.q: Which of the following are the reasons/factors for exposure to benzene pollution ? [2020-I] 1️⃣ Automobile exhaust 2️⃣ Tobacco smoke 3️⃣ Wood burning 4️⃣ Using varnished wooden furniture 5️⃣ Using products made of polyurethane.
questions.e: Benzene pollution comes from industrial sources like automobiles/petroleum, tobacco smoke, and wood burning. It is also released from indoor materials like varnished furniture, plywood, and polyurethane products.

questions.q: With reference to India's Desert National Park, which of the following statements are correct? [2020-I] 1️⃣ It is spread over two districts. 2️⃣ There is no human habitation inside the Park. 3️⃣ It is one of the natural habitats of the Great Indian Bustard.
questions.e: Desert National Park is spread across the Jaisalmer and Barmer districts of Rajasthan and is a home to the Great Indian Bustard. Contrary to some rules, human habitations (villages) do exist inside the park.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2020-I] 1️⃣ 36% of India's districts are classified as "overexploited" or "critical" by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA). 2️⃣ CGWA was formed under the Environment (Protection) Act. 3️⃣ India has the largest area under groundwater irrigation in the world. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The CGWA was established under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. India possesses the world's largest area equipped for groundwater irrigation (approx. 39 million ha).

questions.q: Among the following Tiger Reserves, which one has the largest area under "Critical Tiger Habitat"? [2020-I]
questions.e: Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam has a Critical Tiger Habitat area of approximately 3,721 sq. km, which is larger than that of Sunderbans (approx. 1,699 sq. km) and other reserves.

questions.q: If a particular plant species is placed under Schedule VI of The Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, what is the implication? [2020-I]
o: (d) Such a plant is invasive and harmful to the ecosystem.
(a) A licence is required to cultivate that plant.
(b) Such a plant cannot be cultivated under any circumstances.
(c) It is a Genetically Modified crop plant.
questions.e: Plants listed in Schedule VI (like Beddomes' cycad or Pitcher plant) require a specific license from the Chief Wildlife Warden for cultivation.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements best describes the term 'Social Cost of Carbon'? [2020-I]
o: (a) long-term damage done by a tonne of $CO_{2}$ emissions in a given year.
(b) requirement of fossil fuels for a country to provide goods and services to its citizens
(d) contribution of an individual person to the carbon footprint on the planet Earth.
(c) efforts put in by a climate refugee to adapt to live in a new place.
questions.e: The Social Cost of Carbon is a monetary measure of the long-term damage (net present value of impacts) caused by emitting one additional tonne of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

questions.q: In the context of India, which of the following is/are considered to be practice(s) of eco-friendly agriculture? [2020-I] 1️⃣ Crop diversification 2️⃣ Legume intensification 3️⃣ Tensiometer use 4️⃣ Vertical farming.
questions.e: All these practices are eco-friendly: crop diversification reduces herbicide needs, tensiometers optimize water use, and vertical farming minimizes land and water consumption.

questions.q: With reference to Indian elephants, consider the following statements: [2020-I] 1️⃣ The leader of an elephant group is a female 2️⃣ The maximum gestation period can be 22 months. 3️⃣ An elephant can normally go on calving till the age of 40 years only. 4️⃣ Among the States in India, the highest elephant population is in Kerala.
questions.e: Elephant groups are led by a female 'matriarch' and have a gestation period of up to 22 months. Karnataka (not Kerala) has the highest elephant population in India according to recent data.

questions.q: Which of the following Protected Areas are located in Cauvery basin ? [2020-I] 1️⃣ Nagarhole National park 2️⃣ Papikonda National park 3️⃣ Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve 4️⃣ Wayanad Wildlife sanctuary.
questions.e: Nagarhole (Karnataka), Sathyamangalam (Tamil Nadu), and Wayanad (Kerala) are all within the Cauvery river basin. Papikonda National Park is located in Andhra Pradesh, outside this basin.

questions.q: With reference to India's biodiversity, Ceylon frogmouth, Coppersmith barbet, Gray-chinned minivet and White-throated redstart are [2020-I]
questions.e: These names refer to various species of birds found within India's diverse ecosystems.

questions.q: Which one of the following protected areas is well-known for the conservation of a sub-species of the Indian swamp deer (Barasinga) that thrives well in hard ground and is exclusively graminivorous? [2020-I]
questions.e: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is specifically famous for the conservation of the Barasingha (Swamp deer) subspecies.

questions.q: Which of the following are the most likely places to find the musk deer in its natural habitat? [2020-I] 1️⃣ Askot Wildlife Sanctuary 2️⃣ Gangotri National Park 3️⃣ Kishanpur Wildlife Sanctuary 4️⃣ Manas National Park.
questions.e: Musk deer are found in high-altitude cold Himalayan ecosystems. Askot (Uttarakhand) and Gangotri are suitable habitats, whereas Manas and Kishanpur are at lower altitudes.

questions.q: In rural road construction, the use of which of the following is preferred for ensuring environmental sustainability or to reduce carbon footprint? [2020-I] 1️⃣ Copper slag 2️⃣ Cold mix asphalt technology 3️⃣ Geotextiles 4️⃣ Hot mix asphalt technology 5️⃣ Portland cement.
questions.e: Copper slag (a non-hazardous byproduct), cold mix asphalt, and geotextiles (like coir) are preferred for sustainable road construction. Hot mix technology requires high heating, increasing emissions.
